advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix `_split_name_reason` so a name containing a whitespace-surrounded separator (e.g. ' — ') is not truncated: anchor the reason split to the LAST separator, or key the harvested marker off the detected site's name rather than re-deriving it from the marker text.
evidence: scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:83: `split = _NAME_REASON_RE.search(rest)` — takes the FIRST whitespace-surrounded separator
scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:48: `_NAME_REASON_RE = re.compile(r"\s+(?:" + "|".join(re.escape(s) for s in _SEPARATORS) + r")\s+")` with `_SEPARATORS = ("—", "--", "-", ":")`
.github/workflows/release.yml:93: `- name: Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main` — census key becomes `ci_gate::.github/workflows/release.yml::Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main`

.github/mechanism-baseline.json contains many such names: 'Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main', 'mypy — full library + scripts/ (gating)', 'Diff coverage on changed lines (report-only; Gerrit Verified lane)'
advisory.finding: A `# mechanism-ok:` marker cannot justify any mechanism whose NAME contains a whitespace-surrounded separator (em dash, ' - ', ' : '). `_split_name_reason` splits at the FIRST whitespace-surrounded separator, but that separator can fall inside the name itself — e.g. the ci_gate step name '.github/workflows/release.yml::Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main'. The marker then harvests under the truncated key '...::Guard', which never matches the census key, so the step stays unadmitted. This is the same defect class the ticket comment claims to have fixed for space-containing names, but it was only fixed for the space-token case, not for names that carry their own separator.
scenarios: An author adds/modifies a workflow step whose name contains ' — ' (the house style) and tries to justify it with the documented marker; the gate keeps reporting it as new/unadmitted with no way to satisfy it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Since a marker is harvested from a known site, prefer keying the reason to the site's actual (kind, name) instead of re-parsing the name from the marker text; or split on the LAST whitespace-surrounded separator so trailing reason wins over an in-name separator.

advisory.finding: The env_var detectors fail open: if `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` is absent `detect_env_vars` returns `[]`, and if `rebar._deprecations`/`rebar.mcp_server` cannot be imported `_derived_env_names` returns `{}`. In `--check` a shrunken/empty env_var census buckets the missing names as `stale`, and stale always passes — so a broken detector produces a green gate indistinguishable from 'all env vars removed'. `_run_check` performs no liveness assertion that any detector actually produced results.
scenarios: An environment/import regression breaks the env-registry import path during a real `make lint` run: every REBAR_* var buckets as stale, the gate passes green, and newly added env vars in the same change go undetected.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test harvesting a real `# mechanism-ok: <kind> <name> —` marker (dangling separator, no reason) and assert it does not admit the mechanism.
evidence: tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py:176-182 injects the blank reason directly into `evaluate`'s marker map, bypassing parse_marker entirely.
scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:81-92 `_split_name_reason` is the code that must turn a dangling separator into `""`; no test feeds it such a line.
Named violating input: a marker line `# mechanism-ok: lock foo.lock —` (separator, no reason) harvested via markers_for/parse_marker should yield reason `""` and NOT admit the mechanism.
dropped.finding: The blank-reason contract is verified only at the `evaluate()` layer with pre-built marker dicts (`{"lock::new.lock": ""|"   "}`), never through `parse_marker`/`_split_name_reason` on a real marker line. The newly-added parsing logic that collapses a dangling-separator tail to `""` (markers.py:81-92) — e.g. a source line `# mechanism-ok: lock foo.lock —` with nothing after the separator — is untested, so a regression that parsed such a line as a non-blank reason would admit an unjustified mechanism while the suite stays green.
scenarios: A change to the separator regex or the fallback partition that leaves a stray separator character as the 'reason' would defeat the anti-rubber-stamp guard undetected.
